findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: An attacker-controlled i2caddr value that causes an unexpected behavior in the I2C communication protocol.
findings.assumptions: The I2CSend function is not shown and may internally invoke a command interpreter or perform operations that are vulnerable to command injection.

findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: An attacker-controlled bytes value that exceeds the actual length of the data array.
findings.assumptions: The data array is not checked for length before being accessed in the for loop.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: An attacker-controlled i2caddr value that includes special characters or sequences that are interpreted by the I2C protocol in a way that could lead to unintended command execution.
findings.assumptions: The I2CSend function does not properly sanitize the i2caddr before using it in the I2C communication.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: An attacker-controlled i2caddr value that includes special characters or sequences that are interpreted by the I2C protocol in a way that could lead to unintended command execution.
findings.assumptions: The I2CSend function does not properly sanitize the i2caddr before using it in the I2C communication.
